research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK primary guidance only; higher-risk building control approval, application information, controlled changes and completion-certificate methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Higher-risk building approval threshold
verified_claims: BSR oversees building work for buildings with at least 7 storeys or 18 metres and either 2 residential units, a hospital or a care home.
limitations: The threshold does not determine whether a particular connected structure is one building.

sources.name: Registration before occupation
verified_claims: A higher-risk residential building with at least 2 residential units must be registered before people live there.
limitations: Registration does not prove all building-control or occupation duties are satisfied.

sources.name: Approval assessment purposes
verified_claims: BSR uses an application to assess regulatory compliance, project management and competence appointments.
limitations: Application assessment does not prove completed work will comply.

sources.name: Non-higher-risk building authority
verified_claims: Non-higher-risk building control is normally managed by a local authority or registered building control approver, not BSR.
limitations: Mixed projects can require separate authorities and project-specific confirmation.

sources.name: Client legal responsibility
verified_claims: The client must ensure approval is granted before work starts and application information is correct.
limitations: Authorising an agent does not transfer the client's legal responsibility.

sources.name: Approval before starting work
verified_claims: Required higher-risk building work must not start before BSR approval; unauthorised work can be a criminal offence.
limitations: The rule does not establish that any named project has started unlawfully.

sources.name: Exempt work within wider project
verified_claims: Exempt or competent-person-scheme work must be included when it forms part of a wider project requiring approval.
limitations: A work label alone is not enough to determine exemption.

sources.name: Single and multiple tower applications
verified_claims: A single application may cover a single tower or connected multiple-tower project in specified circumstances.
limitations: Connection and common-part evidence is required to define application scope.

sources.name: Staged application process
verified_claims: Staged applications allow detailed plans to be approved for each stage before that stage starts.
limitations: Staging does not permit work to begin before approval of the relevant stage.

sources.name: Existing-building evidence assessment
verified_claims: Existing-building applications should use surveys, inspections and building information to assess effects and compliance.
limitations: General building age or assumptions cannot replace project-specific evidence.

sources.name: Application assumptions and testing
verified_claims: Unavoidable assumptions must be evidenced and accompanied by a plan to test them during construction.
limitations: An assumption remains unverified until the planned test is completed.

sources.name: Existing-building work categories
verified_claims: Work to an existing higher-risk building is classified as category A or B; using the wrong category may lead to rejection.
limitations: Classification requires the actual work scope and cannot be inferred from a short description.

sources.name: Emergency repair definition
verified_claims: Emergency repair work addresses an urgent health, safety or welfare risk and may proceed promptly under the special process.
limitations: Poor planning or ordinary remedial work should not be treated as an emergency.

sources.name: Emergency notice and regularisation
verified_claims: Emergency repair information must be notified promptly and a regularisation certificate sought after completion.
limitations: Notification and regularisation do not prove the work was compliant or correctly classified.

sources.name: Approval assessment and decisions
verified_claims: Unless extended, assessment can take up to 12 weeks for new buildings and 8 weeks for existing buildings, with approval, conditional approval or rejection outcomes.
limitations: Published time limits are not guarantees for a specific application.
